newsitem.title: USA: Brooklyn Union holding company plan approved.
newsitem.headline: Brooklyn Union holding company plan approved.

text.p: Brooklyn Union Gas Co said the New York Public Service Commission has approved the utility's plant to reorganize its gas-distribution operations and kits subsidiaries into a holding company.
This was the "major" regulatory hurdle the proposal faced, President Craig G. Matthews told Reuters.
He noted it must still be approved by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, which is not expected to be a problem now that state regulators have cleared the proposal.
The company said it expects to present the plan to shareholders at their meeting in February.
It said the holding company will be named KeySpan Energy Corp and expects to trade in the New York Stock Exchange with the symbol KY.

Matthews said the commission approval gives Brooklyn Union operating flexibilities even if the proposal is not accepted by shareholders, explaining the company could go ahead with most of its proposals without the holding company structure.
One of the changes approved by the commission allows the utility to offer additional services to customers, he said, explaining this would be similar to telephone companies offering call waiting.

Pointing out the company does not know the value of such services, Matthews said the possibilities include bill consolidations for property managers with more than one address in the company's service area and offering maintenance services -- on a contract or spot basis -- on other than gas appliances.
Such service might have to be offered by a subsidiary other than the utility, he said, noting regulators' reluctance to allow regulated utilities compete with other service providers.
Other things being considered, he said, include energy use monitoring for individual homes or businesses, which could lead to provision of billing data to other suppliers at the location.
Matthews said Brooklyn Union is now piloting a program with Microsoft Corp but declined to discuss the technology being used.

Brooklyn Union said the commision action allows the company to increase its non-utility investments to as much as 50 percent of capitalization over the next five years from the current 15 percent cap.
"We don't plan on getting there immediately," Matthews said, noting the company has said it expects to have 50 percent of profits from non-utility sources within five years.

The needed investments "will require some external capital," he said, adding this will be provided by subsidiary borrowings and KeySpan equity sales. The holding company will not hold debt directly, he said.

Noting Brooklyn Union's belief its stock does not reflect the value of such operations as Houston Exploration, Matthews said this will "no longer be an academic argument" once Houston completes its initial offering and begins trading.
He said the company expects analysts to compare KeySpan with MCN Corp and Questar Corp once the holding company is formed.
Brooklyn Union, the utility, will be the major subsidiary of the holding company, the company's statement pointed out.

The proposal approved by regulators includes a multi-year rate agreement that will provide greater pricing flexibility. After an initial reduction in 1997, the non-gas -- or transportation -- component in customer bills will be under specific price caps through the year 2002.
Brooklyn Union said it "is the first energy utility in the country to reach a price-cap plan with a state utility commission."
Under the terms of the rate plan, Brooklyn Union's gas-distribution operations will continue to be regulated by the state commission as they always have been, it noted.
Matthews said, "The new plan provides us with a clear incentive to enhance revenues and control costs.
"We are confident and optimistic that under this price-cap form of regulation, we will continue to improve our record of financial performance."
